text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A sharp rise in Nigerian demand for foreign exchange may be driven by speculation of a possible devaluation of the naira.

- Military top brass on Thursday visited Warri to assess the damage done to property during communal clashes. The team visited crude oil terminals belonging to the Nigerian producing units of Royal Dutch Shell and Chevron .
- Eastern Enugu state says it has reserves of clay, kaolin, pyrites, iron, limestone and silica which could all be exploited commercially if the necessary investment were supplied.
- Oluwa Glass plans to raise 450 million naira to finance reconstruction of a 700 million naira furnace.
- Plans are underway to create a commission which would regulate public enterprises and arrange for the prosecution of those accused of playing a part in the near collapse of some enterprises.

- The inability of The Nigerian Unity Line shipping company to pay 14 million naira in fees to the Securities and Exchange Commission has stalled its plans to raise one billion naira through the capital market.

- A major crash of share prices is imminent as speculative investors who moved to the stock market after the fall in money market rates in February begin divesting. As money market rates have now improved some major blue chip shares are among those that stand to lose.
- Petroleum marketing companies have allayed fears of renewed fuel shortages and say queues at petrol stations are only symptoms of panic buying.
